events.excerpt: One nice thing about discovering exoplanets is that, once you work out how long their orbits take, they continue to show up like clockwork. The timing is so regular, in fact, that we can use variations to detect the gravitational influence of additional planets in the same exosolar system. And the precise timing is useful in that we can rely on it to point telescopes at the system when we know some of the light we detect has passed through the planet's atmosphere. Except when we can't. On Monday, researchers reported on an exoplanet that simply stopped showing up. TOI-2535b is a hot Jupiter-sized planet we've been observing as it transits between its host star, TOI-2535, and Earth for about seven years now. But it recently stopped showing up, and researchers suspect that's due to an unseen companion orbiting in a different plane. Read full article Comments
events.headline: The amazing disappearing exoplanet

events.excerpt: Description A few small nit cleanups on the synchronizer component in consensus. Behavior change: fetch_blocks_from_peers now returns as soon as no request is in flight, instead of idling until the 4s FETCH_FROM_PEERS_TIMEOUT. This affects two cases: no request was sent because every selected block was already locked, or the last outstanding request failed with no peer left to retry on. In both cases no further network request is sent, and a failed request still waits the full 2s request timeout, so periodic runs cannot repeat faster than every ~2s on failures. The only new cost is local: while all selected blocks are locked, the scheduler polls get_missing_blocks at its default 200ms cadence instead of every 4s, which is the same cadence it already uses during fast successful sync. Added a test covering both cases. Test plan CI/PT Release notes Check each box that your changes affect. If none of the boxes relate to your changes, release notes aren't required. For each box you select, include information after the relevant heading that describes the impact of your changes that a user might notice and any actions they must take to implement updates. Protocol: Nodes (Validators and Full nodes): gRPC: JSON-RPC: GraphQL: CLI: Rust SDK: Indexing Framework: Co-authored-by: Claude Fable

events.excerpt: Bitcoin Magazine Israel Discount Bank to Let Customers Trade Bitcoin in App Starting Nov. 26 Israel Discount Bank said Wednesday that from Nov. 26 it will let eligible customers buy, hold and sell bitcoin and ether in the bank’s mobile app, a launch that would beat larger rival Bank Leumi if it stays on schedule. The Tel Aviv-listed lender described the service as a first for Israel’s banking system in a Nov. 11 statement. Customers will be able to trade the two assets alongside stocks and bonds, without opening an account at an outside exchange or managing a separate digital wallet. The offer is limited to private, not corporate, customers who are Israeli residents, 18 or older, and whose accounts are already set up for securities trading, subject to the bank’s terms. “For the first time in the banking system, Discount Bank will allow trading in digital currencies directly from the bank account in a simple and secure manner, without the need for complex dedicated digital wallets,” Avi Levi, CEO of Discount Group, said in the statement. “This is a first step toward establishing advanced technological infrastructure in the digital currency space and developing the bank’s capabilities in this area.” The rollout was led by Elad Fisher, head of the bank’s financial markets division.

The issue affects images rendered with a height or width of zero at the selected printing resolution. These might not be visible to users, but can form part of a document's watermarking or layout. After the update, those invisible objects can apparently make the printed document disappear too. Microsoft said: "The issue was observed when printing Microsoft Word documents using the Windows Graphics Device Interface (GDI), but printing from other applications might also be affected." According to the notification (WI1549472), most versions of Windows are affected, from the latest Windows 11 26H2 through Windows 10 Enterprise LTSC 2016. Windows Server from 2025 to 2016 is also affected. Users need not have added these objects themselves. Microsoft says document-generation tools can insert them even when no graphic is visible. events.excerpt: A Democratic takeover of Congress may look like bad news for the industry, but Bitwise Chief Investment Officer Matt Hougan believes the bigger picture tells a different story. Importance of Demographics The latest election put Democrats in control of both houses of Congress, with Elizabeth Warren likely to become chair of the Senate Banking Committee. Given her history of opposing crypto, the development has raised concerns about what could come next for the industry. Hougan, however, does not see the election as a major setback. According to the lobbying group Stand With Crypto, the incoming Senate has 51 pro-crypto members, compared with 52 in the outgoing Congress. In the House, at least 241 members have received an A or B rating on crypto policy, which gives them a solid majority in the 425-member caucus. events.excerpt: [Nozomi] travels with a Nintendo Switch 2, but the official dock is bulky and doesn’t seem to be made for travel. USB-C hubs with displays are common, but they won’t work with the Switch. Not without a little hacking , anyway. It was obvious that the hub wasn’t too far off. It will charge the Switch, so Power Delivery was working. A sniffer showed that even the DisplayPort initialization happened. A little flashing on the hub allowed it to complete the proprietary protocol, and that made TV mode work, but HDR was washed out. [Nozomi] theorized it was a mismatched color space, so that required a patch for a different chip. Another flash forces the right color tag for HDR TV, but there would have to be another patch for HDR DP. That patch doesn’t exist. Variable refresh rate also does not work. We didn’t find the actual code for the patches, but we still thought the detective work was worth the read. Some people don’t want a more portable dock, but a less portable one .
events.headline: USB-C Hub or Nintendo Switch 2 Dock? Relax, It’s Both!

events.excerpt: Japan is considering penalties for AI companies that ignore government orders. The penalties will be aimed mostly at U.S. developers of advanced AI, whose systems Japan uses but cannot force to share information. Officials plan to publish a full reform blueprint before the end of 2026. Why can’t Japan make American AI companies cooperate? Japan’s AI Promotion Act , which states that if AI misuse harms someone’s rights, the government can investigate and give guidance, took full effect in September 2025. But the law has no punishment for a company that simply refuses to cooperate. Japan is now considering including penalties in its law. This regulatory gap is a bigger problem with foreign companies. A group within Japan’s ruling Liberal Democratic Party, led by former digital minister Masaaki Taira, warned in a draft proposal that other governments can get information from AI companies, but Japan may not be able to. The draft noted that the European Union already fines AI companies that refuse to hand over information. Japan is most worried about advanced AI that it does not build or control. events.excerpt: Ethereum researchers are proposing a major change to the network’s development priorities, stepping away from plans to introduce faster block production in favor of accelerating protections against quantum computing and artificial intelligence threats. Research group Ethlabs announced that it would withdraw its Quick Slots proposal from Ethereum’s planned Hegotá upgrade, redirecting its resources toward a new security roadmap called pqai27 . The initiative aims to make Ethereum’s core infrastructure and user accounts more resistant to emerging cryptographic threats by 2027. The proposal reflects growing concerns that advances in quantum computing and AI could eventually undermine the cryptographic systems protecting digital assets. Although no existing quantum computer can currently break Ethereum’s security, researchers argue that replacing the network’s underlying cryptography could take years.
